newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal says telecoms sale to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Senegal says telecoms sale to go ahead.

text.p: Senegal said on Tuesday it would press ahead with the sale of its state telecommunications company SONATEL and a privatisation official said talks with a Swedish-led consortium were almost complete.

Senegal's communication minister, Serigne Diop, who is also the government spokesman, told state radio he had heard nothing to suggest problems with a provisional deal for the consortium led by Telia Overseas of Sweden to buy a one third stake.
"Nothing can compromise the privatisation of SONATEL, entered into by the government and its social partners," he added.
Abdoulaye Cisse, a member of the panel handling Senegal's state portofolio, said talks were drawing to a close.

"We are about to finalise contract procedures with Telia," he told Reuters. "We are moving forward in the discussions. It's better we take the time we need, instead of making mistakes by speeding up in the talks."
Last November, Senegal signed a provisional deal with the consortium for it to pay up to 70 billion CFA francs, representing one third of the projected capital of SONATEL.
Other members of the consortium include the Walter Group of the United States, China Telecommunication Services and private Senegalese company Senecom Partners.
The remaining shares will be sold to private Senegalese and African investors with 10 percent allocated to SONATEL staff. It was not immediately clear how the shares would be marketed.
A source close to SONATEL's management said the consortium planned to invest 150 billion CFA in the West African nation's telecommunications sector.
The government, which initially thought the sale would raise just 70 billion CFA francs, now expects to make 210 billion CFA francs.

SONATEL staff favour the privatisation policy, but want to pay less for their stake than the government is asking -- 10 percent of 50 billion CFA francs instead of 10 percent of 70 billion CFA francs, the initially projected price.
"We seeking a reaction from the president or a positive response of the economy ministry, otherwise SONATEL will be in turmoil," SONATEL union leader Ibrahima Konte said.
SONATEL currently has capital of 50 billion CFA francs and an annual turnover of more than 60 billion CFA francs.
